hints: Look first at the two key regions in every IR spectrum, the $\text{O-H}$ stretch around 2500 to 3500 $cm^{-1}$ and the $\text{C=O}$ stretch around 1700 $cm^{-1}$.
Spectrum 1 shows a very sharp, strong $\text{C=O}$ peak but no broad $\text{O-H}$ dip, so it can only be the molecule with a carbonyl and no $\text{O-H}$ group.

Compare the broad $\text{O-H}$ dips in spectra 2 and 3, the very broad one covering 2500 to 3300 $cm^{-1}$ plus $\text{C=O}$ belongs to the acid, while the cleaner broad peak near 3300 $cm^{-1}$ with no $\text{C=O}$ belongs to the alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Recall the fingerprint IR absorptions**

Think like a detective. Three functional groups give three clear clues.

$$\text{C=O in ketone or acid} \approx 1700 \text{ to } 1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (sharp, strong)}$$ $$\text{O-H in alcohol} \approx 3200 \text{ to } 3600 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (broad)}$$ $$\text{O-H in carboxylic acid} \approx 2500 \text{ to } 3300 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (very broad, overlapping C-H)}$$

**Analyse spectrum 1**

Spectrum 1 has a tall sharp dip at about 1700 $cm^{-1}$. That is $\text{C=O}$.

But look above 3000 $cm^{-1}$. There is no broad $\text{O-H}$ dip, only small sharp $\text{C-H}$ peaks near 3000 $cm^{-1}$. No $\text{O-H}$ plus $\text{C=O}$ means a ketone. That is propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$.

**Analyse spectrum 2**

Spectrum 2 also has a strong $\text{C=O}$ dip near 1700 $cm^{-1}$.

But it also has a huge, very broad dip from about 2500 to 3300 $cm^{-1}$ that swallows the $\text{C-H}$ region. That very broad $\text{O-H}$ plus $\text{C=O}$ together is the classic signature of a carboxylic acid. That is propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.

**Analyse spectrum 3 and conclude**

Spectrum 3 has a broad smooth dip centred near 3350 $cm^{-1}$ but no strong peak near 1700 $cm^{-1}$.

Broad $\text{O-H}$ with no $\text{C=O}$ means an alcohol. That is propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. So the order is spectrum 1 propanone, spectrum 2 propanoic acid, spectrum 3 propan-2-ol.

options.A: Incorrect. Spectrum 1 cannot be propanoic acid because it lacks the very broad acid $\text{O-H}$ absorption from 2500 to 3300 $cm^{-1}$. A sharp $\text{C=O}$ alone points to the ketone, not the acid.
options.B: Correct. Spectrum 1 is propanone with $\text{C=O}$ and no $\text{O-H}$, spectrum 2 is propanoic acid with both $\text{C=O}$ and very broad $\text{O-H}$, spectrum 3 is propan-2-ol with broad alcoholic $\text{O-H}$ and no $\text{C=O}$. This matches all three IR fingerprints perfectly.
options.C: Incorrect. Spectrum 2 is not propan-2-ol because it clearly shows a strong $\text{C=O}$ peak near 1700 $cm^{-1}$, which an alcohol does not have. Spectrum 3 is not the acid because it has no $\text{C=O}$ peak.
options.D: Incorrect. Spectrum 1 is not propan-2-ol because it has a strong $\text{C=O}$ peak and no broad $\text{O-H}$ peak. Spectrum 3 is not propanone because it has a broad $\text{O-H}$ peak and no $\text{C=O}$ peak. The two have been swapped.
